proposed_facts.reason: Canonical lifecycle callbacks explicitly select thrown state 3 and dropped state 4. DmgDealt invokes the bounce helper only for those states and returns false unconditionally.
Table rows 3 and 4 share the same physics callback, whose body applies falling physics. ThrownDropped meaningfully improves the rendered Thrown-only name without claiming original spelling.
Table rows 1, 3 and 4 register this animation callback; its complete body only returns false.

State-1 setup and falling physics, together with explicit thrown/dropped transitions, establish all three dispatch contexts. The inert callback performs none of the separately implemented emission, accounting or damage work.

Canonical setup resets velocity and selects state 0. Both released-state collision callbacks use the exact nonzero guard, while zero propagates the alternative collision result. Contextual collision code confirms qualified landing dispatch and the guarded supported-terrain callback from state 5.

contradictions.reason: Accept deferral of all three .sdata2 claims: the reset call establishes source behavior, not compiled section attribution, size or constant placement. No compiled claim is promoted.
Resolve the formerly uncertain thrown/dropped identification: the named lifecycle callbacks explicitly select states 3 and 4, matching the damage callback guard.
Resolve the physics-name mismatch and both one-state animation descriptions using actual table registrations, rather than numeric symbol suffixes or rendered hypotheses.

Resolve the omitted dropped-state reset caller while preserving negative/nonzero counters, zero-counter bypass and conditional landing behavior. State 5 likewise supplies a guarded supported-terrain callback, not an unconditional transition.

Accept deferral of literal sixteen-shot capacity: initialization loads an attribute rather than a literal capacity. Preserve the documentary claim as unresolved, not source-proven. The local positive-only decrement and unconditional companion-constructor call remain supported.
